english.title: Store body for anatomical examination without death certificate - Human Tissue Act 2004
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) did an activity to which section 1(2) of the Human Tissue Act 2004 applied, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACTIVITY..), without a certificate under section 22(1) of the Births and Deaths Registration Act 1953 or Article 25(2) of the Births and Deaths Registration (Northern Ireland) Order 1976 having been signed in relation to the cause of death of the person concerned
english.legislation: Contrary to section 5(3) and (7) of the Human Tissue Act 2004.

english.notes:
Section 5(4) of the Human Tissue Act 2004 provides that the offence does not apply
(a) where the person reasonably believes that a certificate under either of the above mentioned provisions has been signed in relation to the cause of death of the person concerned, OR that what he does is not an activity to which section 1(2) of the Human Tissue Act 2004 applies, OR
(b) where the person comes into lawful possession of the body immediately after death and stores it prior to its removal to a place where anatomical examination is to take place.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
